title: Control evidence
description: What the attest step recorded about each requirement: the result of each half of each control's paired proof, each setting read from the hosting platform, and each finding of the audit report, together with a digest of what defined the checks when it was recorded. The file is written by `lisa controls attest` and is never edited by hand; `lisa controls attest --check` computes the verdict again from it, takes the same digest from the repository as it is, and fails when the committed verdict differs or the checks are no longer what was proved.

schema_version.description: The version of this format. It changes only when a reader written for the previous version would misread the file.

checks.description: What defined the checks at the run that wrote the file. A file without it was written before evidence was bound to what defines the checks, and is not read as evidence.

records.description: One record per result per requirement, ordered by `id`. A result about a control that serves two requirements is two records.

criterion_id.description: A requirement id as the specification writes it, for example `AC5.4` or `SI7`.

utc_time.description: A time in UTC with milliseconds, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`.

sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest, in lower-case hexadecimal.

checks.description: One digest over everything that defines the checks, and the list of what it covers: the `gates` block of `.lisa.config.json`, every file under `.lisa/controls/proofs/`, `.lisa/controls/carriers.json` with every file it lists and every file under `.lisa/hooks/`, the gate runner under `scripts/`, and the repository's own hook files that hold Lisa's marked call. Each file is read in the copy the proofs ran in, so the digest is of what was proved. A checked tool's own configuration is not covered.

covered.description: Everything the digest covers, each file once, ordered by `path`.

digest.description: The SHA-256 digest of `covered` written as canonical JSON: object keys in code-unit order, no spaces, the list in its own order.

covered_file.description: One thing that defines the checks, and the digest of its content.

path.description: The file, from the repository root. For `.lisa.config.json` the digest is of its `gates` block in canonical form and not of the whole file, so a change to another setting there is not a change to a check.

sha256.description: The digest of the file's content.

record.description: One of three kinds of record, told apart by `rung`.

exercised_record.description: One half of a paired proof: a change was planted and the control's answer recorded.

checks_digest.description: The digest of what defined the checks when the record was made: the `digest` of the file's `checks` at the run that wrote it. A record that carries another digest counts for nothing.

command.description: What was started, one item per argument, or `null` when nothing was.

commit.description: The commit the attest run's disposable copy was cloned from. A record written when nothing was cloned names the commit the repository was at. `null` when the repository has no commit or is not a git repository. It is information for a reader: nothing is decided by it, and it need not exist in the clone the file is read in.

completed_at.description: When its answer was in, in UTC. The freshness lifetime is counted from here.

criterion.description: The requirement the record is evidence for.

detail.description: The same as a sentence. On a `not-applicable` record it is the fact that makes the requirement not apply.

entry_id.description: The identifier of the register entry the record is about, for example `code-style@api`.

exit_status.description: The exit status of what was started, or `null` when nothing ran to an end.

freshness_seconds.description: How long after `completed_at` the record states it may be relied on, in whole seconds; never more than twelve months. A record is relied on for thirty days at most, whatever it states. Past that, the requirement reads `unknown`.

half.description: Which half: the change that breaks the rule, or the one that does not. Only an exercised record names a half.

id.description: The record's identifier, unique in the file. It is made only of what the record is about: `<entry id>/<moment>/<half or rung>/<requirement>` for a record about a control, `audit-finding/<requirement>@<folder>` for a record of an audit finding. No time and no counter goes into it, so the same proof of the same control has the same identifier on every run.

moment.description: The moment the record speaks for: `commit`, `push`, `pull-request`.

output_excerpt.description: The end of what the check printed; empty when nothing ran.

output_truncated.description: Whether the excerpt leaves out earlier output.

reason.description: A short, fixed word for why the record shows what it does: the proof's reason, or the audit finding's state.

result.description: `held`: the control did what the requirement asks. `failed`: it did not. `unknown`: there is no answer that can be relied on.

rung.description: A change was planted and the control's answer recorded.

scope.description: The folder the record is about, written from the repository root, or `.` for the whole repository.

started_at.description: When the record's check began, in UTC.

observed_record.description: A setting read from the system that holds it, with nothing planted.

reason.description: A short, fixed word for why the record shows what it does: the proof's reason, or the audit finding's state.

result.description: `held`: the record was found where the audit pointed, or a person's answer vouches for it, or (for a requirement a check answers, which this never satisfies) the audit found something. `failed`: the audit found nothing that does it. `unknown`: the audit could not establish it, the record was not where it pointed, or no person has answered. `not-applicable`: the requirement does not apply, and `detail` is the fact that makes it so.

rung.description: `asserted`: the finding, or a person's answer to the audit's question, is said and not checked. `observed`: the finding is about a record that exists, and the attest step found the file and line the audit pointed at. That shows the record is there, not that it says what the requirement asks.

scope.description: The folder the record is about, written from the repository root, or `.` for the whole repository.

started_at.description: When the record's check began, in UTC.
